equity_bridge.note: USD 480m at 1.1257 = EUR 426m, paid post-balance-sheet, non-recurring so not in the flows

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 3.5% vs revenue 7.6% and EPS 46.6%: book value is depressed by the EUR 3.1bn FY2024 restructuring charge, EUR 2.7bn/yr dividends and buybacks, so it is not a usable growth proxy here. EPS 3yr CAGR is off the FY2022 trough (EUR 1.95, Qualtrics/venture write-downs) and is meaningless. Revenue 3yr CAGR 7.6% is the cleanest historical anchor; the forward base path starts above it (10%) because FY2026 guidance and the +27% cloud backlog say so, and converges below it by year 8.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC; interest income not stripped, see inputs.notes). Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR 4.9% vs reported 5.7%: SBC expense grew from EUR 1,084m (FY2020) to EUR 1,695m (FY2025, and EUR 2,385m in FY2024), i.e. faster than cash flow, so part of the reported growth was paid for in stock-linked compensation. The 3yr figures are distorted by the FY2022 base (FY2022 FCF EUR 4.8bn was depressed by Qualtrics and restructuring) and the FY2025 peak (first clean post-restructuring year).

scenario_narratives.base: SAP converts the bulk of its ~35,000-customer ECC base to S/4HANA Cloud through the Dec-2027 maintenance cliff: cloud grows ~24% in FY2026 and stays above 15% through FY2028 while support (-7%/yr) and licences (-25%/yr) shrink to a remainder, so total revenue compounds ~10% for two years then decelerates to GDP-plus by year 8. The +27% current cloud backlog underwrites the first two years. Operating leverage arrives as management says it will -- the AI/R&D investment phase is temporary -- taking pre-SBC EBITDA from 34.5% to 41% by FY2032, but no faster, because the cloud mix dilutes gross margin and SAP has to keep buying data/AI capabilities (Dremio, Reltio, Prior Labs) to stay credible in agentic workflows. Business AI/Joule and Business Data Cloud expand wallet share modestly rather than transformatively. Regulatory matters (EU probe, DOJ, Celonis trial Dec-2026) cost money and management time but do not change the maintenance model.
scenario_narratives.bull: The migration wave is larger and stickier than the base assumes: SI capacity holds, agent-led migration tooling cuts conversion effort ~35%, and the ~60% of ECC customers who had not started by 2025 overwhelmingly stay with SAP rather than defecting to Oracle Fusion or Workday. Business AI/BDC, already in >90% of top-50 deals, becomes a priced layer on top of core ERP, so cloud growth holds above 20% into FY2028 and total revenue compounds 11-12% for three years. Margins expand ~1.5pp/yr to a 44% pre-SBC EBITDA plateau -- still shy of Oracle/Microsoft -- as AI tooling costs normalise and R&D ratios revert. Deferred-revenue capture runs at 15% on the stronger bookings. Terminal growth 3.0% reflects a durable recurring base with pricing power. The SaaSpocalypse narrative proves wrong for systems-of-record ERP, where seats are not the pricing unit.
scenario_narratives.bear: Agentic AI compresses per-seat SaaS economics industry-wide and SAP's cloud pricing power erodes; SI capacity bottlenecks ahead of 2027 push a meaningful minority of ECC customers to extended maintenance, third-party support (helped by an adverse EU Commission or DOJ outcome on maintenance practices) or to Oracle/Workday/Microsoft, so cloud growth fades to the low teens by FY2028 while the legacy decline continues unabated. Total revenue growth drops from 9% to 3% within four years and sits at 2.5% by year 8. The AI investment phase is not temporary: margins stall at ~37% pre-SBC EBITDA, SBC stays at 4.6% of revenue, and continued bolt-on M&A dilutes further. The Celonis antitrust trial forces changes to data-access and bundling practices. Terminal growth 2.0% and a 15x cap reflect a mature, slower franchise.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SAP is valued as a stream of owner free cash flow in EUR -- SBC charged once in the flows at the IFRS 2 expense, leases as an operating cost, share count flat, WACC built from Bund yields -- and converted to USD at spot for comparison with the NYSE ADR. The business is a high-switching-cost systems-of-record franchise mid-way through a forced on-premise-to-cloud migration that ends in Dec-2027, so the near-term path is unusually visible (backlog, guidance) and the long-term question is what the franchise earns once the migration is done and whether agentic AI changes how enterprise software is priced. The scenarios differ on three axes: how much of the ECC base SAP keeps, where pre-SBC margins plateau (37% / 41% / 44%), and the terminal growth and cap that follow from the AI-pricing debate. One discount rate across all scenarios; risk is in the weights and the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin plateau assumption: each 1pp of mature pre-SBC EBITDA margin is worth roughly EUR 4-5/share; management has declined to raise FY2026 profit guidance despite revenue beats
Terminal value is the majority of EV at an 8.5% WACC; a 1pp move in WACC or 0.5pp in terminal growth moves the base value by double digits (see sensitivity grid)
Balance-sheet anchors are FY2025 (2025-12-31); H1-2026 acquisitions, dividend, Teradata settlement and buybacks are only partly reflected via equity_bridge until the H1 report is extracted

SBC settlement mechanics: SAP's awards are largely cash-settled and mark-to-market, so the IFRS 2 expense (and hence the 4.5% SBC charge) swings with the share price; the house last_fcf also double-counts the cash-settled portion for FY2025 (see inputs.notes)

D&A split, lease payments and the diluted share count are reasoned from XBRL totals and public disclosure, not read off extracted filing text -- each could be off by a few tenths of a percent of revenue
EUR/USD: the ADR value moves 1:1 with the rate; at 1.20 (the 52-week high) the same EUR value is ~6.6% higher in USD
Regulatory outcomes (EU Commission, DOJ, Celonis) could force changes to maintenance and data-access practices that the bear case only partly prices

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, NYSE ADR regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 144.97-281.37 USD. Frankfurt SAP.DE close and Yahoo EURUSD=X used for the parity check recorded in inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: research/SAP/Reports/SAP_Metrics.csv -- SEC XBRL IFRS taxonomy data from the 20-F filings, FY2015-FY2025, EUR, converted from whole euros to millions here. No extracted filing text exists for this ticker.
data_sources.qualitative: research/SAP/Reports/SAP_Analysis.json (2026-10-04): business model, revenue mix, Q2-2026 guidance, recent developments, bull/bear cases, risks.

inputs.share_count_basis: Shares outstanding net of treasury, ~1,166m implied by FY2025 net income EUR 7,161m / basic EPS EUR 6.14; diluted ~1,167m (SAP's dilutive effect is negligible, awards are mostly cash-settled). NOT the 1,229m issued-share figure the XBRL SharesOutstanding column carries, which ignores ~62m treasury shares. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the EUR 10bn buyback announced Feb-2026 is the cash mechanism that funds the flat count and is value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL IFRS share-based payment expense (cash-flow add-back) via SAP_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp FY2025 = EUR 1,695m (FY2024 EUR 2,385m; the drop reflects mark-to-market on cash-settled awards after the 2025 share-price fall). SAP publishes no combined figure including equity-award taxes, and no separate equity-award tax line, so the add-back is used unadjusted.
inputs.buyback_note: Financing-activity repurchases for FY2025 are not carried in the XBRL pull, so 0 is recorded (conservative). SAP ran a EUR 5bn programme 2023-2025 to service share-based awards and announced a EUR 10bn programme in Feb-2026; authorised is not spent, and buybacks are value-neutral under the flat-count rule regardless.
inputs.fx_note: EUR->USD 1.1257, Yahoo EURUSD=X close 2026-10-02T21:29Z. Parity check against the Frankfurt primary listing: SAP.DE EUR 183.92 (2026-10-02 close) x 1.1257 = USD 207.04 vs NYSE ADR USD 208.57 (-0.7%), confirming direction (multiply EUR values by fx_rate), 1 ADR = 1 ordinary share, and that the ADR is quoted in whole dollars. All flows, WACC and per-share values are built in EUR; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry prices are in USD (quote currency) and the EUR twins carry the _eur suffix.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Friday; valuation dated Saturday 2026-10-04, no newer session)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the currency of the flows: 10y Bund ~2.7%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.1 (software, large-cap) gives cost of equity ~8.2%; SAP is funded almost entirely by equity (EUR 6.2bn gross debt, net cash) so WACC ~= cost of equity. Rounded up to 8.5% as a single rate across all three scenarios -- risk is charged in the probability-weighted flows, not stacked on the discount rate. Compare the 10.5% USD tech default: the ~2pp gap is the EUR-USD rate differential plus SAP's lower beta.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: a lease charge of 1.0% of revenue (SAP's lease payments run ~EUR 0.4bn/yr; SAP's own free-cash-flow definition deducts them, which is why SAP reported ~EUR 8.0bn FY2025 FCF against the EUR 8.4bn OCF-less-capex in the CSV) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and D&A for the tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation (2.8% of revenue vs ~3.8% all-in). total_debt of EUR 6,150m is read as bonds/borrowings only, so lease liabilities are excluded from net debt, consistent with (B). Check: adj EBITDA 34.5% - SBC 4.6% - lease 1.0% - D&A ex-ROU 2.8% = 26.1% = reported FY2025 IFRS operating margin (EUR 9,617m / 36,800m).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial at SAP (<0.5% of equity); attributable and consolidated flows are treated as identical, no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 1, operating SaaS/enterprise software), with the owner-fcf-adaptations currency rule applied because the filer reports EUR and the ADR quotes USD. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). DATA: SEC XBRL IFRS pull only -- no extracted filing text -- so component anchors (D&A split, lease payments, cash tax paid, diluted count) are reasoned from the CSV and SAP's public disclosures and are flagged as such. SBC SETTLEMENT CAVEAT: SAP's share-based awards are predominantly cash-settled, so the cash paid to settle them already sits inside reported OCF; the house last_fcf (reported FCF - SBC expense = EUR 6,722m) therefore double-counts the cash-settled portion for FY2025 and understates owner cash generation by up to ~EUR 1-1.5bn. The forward build is unaffected: adj_ebitda is pre-SBC (IFRS OP + D&A + SBC expense) and the IFRS 2 expense is charged exactly once through sbc_pct_path, which is the right economic cost whichever way SAP chooses to settle. INTEREST INCOME: net cash EUR 2.1bn is ~0.3x the FCF base, well under the 1x materiality rule, so interest income is left in (it is in financial income, outside EBIT, so it is excluded from the component build anyway). ANCHOR VINTAGE: price is the 2026-10-02 close; balance sheet and share count are FY2025 (2025-12-31, the latest 20-F). H1-2026 moved the balance sheet -- May dividend EUR 2.35/sh (~EUR 2.7bn), Reltio ~EUR 1.0bn, Prior Labs ~EUR 0.65bn, Dremio (undisclosed), Teradata settlement USD 480m, and buybacks under the EUR 10bn programme, against ~EUR 5bn of H1 FCF -- so the three disclosed acquisition/settlement cash costs are deducted in equity_bridge; the remainder is unquantified until the H1-2026 report is extracted and is worth <1% of EV either way. GUIDANCE (Q2-2026, July 2026): cloud revenue EUR 25.8-26.2bn cc (+23-25%), non-IFRS operating profit EUR 11.8-12.2bn cc (includes SBC since 2020; excludes restructuring and acquisition-related charges), FCF ~EUR 10bn (after cash SBC settlements and lease payments), current cloud backlog +27% at Q2.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +10%: guidance cloud EUR 26.0bn mid (+24%) + support -7% (~EUR 9.9bn) + licences -25% (~EUR 0.8bn) + services ~flat (~EUR 4.3bn) = ~EUR 41bn, +11% cc less ~1pp reported FX headwind from the stronger 2026 euro. FY2027 +10% on the +27% current cloud backlog and the Dec-2027 ECC maintenance cliff pulling conversions forward. Decelerates from FY2028 as the forced-migration wave passes and the legacy support base shrinks to a remainder; converges to 3.5% by year 10, 1pp above terminal.
base.margin_rationale: adj EBITDA is pre-SBC, pre-lease, IFRS-16 basis. FY2025 actual 34.5% (IFRS OP 26.1% + SBC 4.6% + D&A 3.8%). FY2026 36.5% is backed out of guidance: non-IFRS OP EUR 12.0bn mid on ~EUR 40.5bn = 29.6%, less ~1.2pp acquisition-related/restructuring to IFRS OP ~28.4%, plus SBC 4.5% and D&A 3.7% (incl. ROU) = 36.6%. Expansion ~1pp/yr to 41% by FY2032 (IFRS EBIT ex-SBC ~34%), still below Oracle/Microsoft's mid-40s non-GAAP margins, reflecting the cloud-mix drag on gross margin (cloud ~75% GM vs support ~90%) offset by R&D/S&M leverage once AI investment normalises as management guides.
base.tax_rationale: SAP's IFRS effective tax rate runs 25-28% (German statutory ~30% diluted by the global mix); 27% flat on positive EBIT. No NOLs or one-off credits to ramp from.
base.wc_rationale: Cloud subscriptions are billed in advance, so deferred revenue grows with bookings; 10% capture of the YoY revenue increase (~EUR 0.3-0.4bn/yr early) is the conservative end of the 15-20% typical for prepaid SaaS, because SAP's receivables and the shrinking prepaid support base partly offset. It shrinks automatically as growth decelerates.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20%: the regulatory overhang is unusually broad for the sector (EU Commission probe, DOJ overcharging inquiry, Celonis trial Dec-2026) and all three point at the maintenance/data-access practices that make the installed base captive, while the SaaSpocalypse repricing is a live sector narrative rather than a hypothetical. Bull trimmed from 35% to 30% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- SI capacity, AI monetisation at scale, and margin expansion management has so far declined to raise guidance for. Base 50%: the ECC cliff is a time-boxed, largely captive tailwind and the +27% backlog has already been booked.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
